title: Supreme Court Upholds Birthright Citizenship, Strikes Down Trump Executive Order
detail: The Supreme Court ruled 6-3 in Trump v. Barbara that the 14th Amendment's Citizenship Clause guarantees automatic birthright citizenship to children born in the US regardless of parents' immigration status, striking down Trump's Executive Order 14160. Chief Justice Roberts wrote the majority opinion, joined by Barrett, Kavanaugh, Sotomayor, Jackson, and Kagan, affirming the 1898 Wong Kim Ark precedent. Justices Thomas, Alito, and Gorsuch dissented.

media.caption: Supreme Court rules 6-3 to uphold birthright citizenship, striking down Trump's executive order

title: Supreme Court Upholds State Bans on Transgender Athletes in Girls' School Sports
detail: In consolidated cases West Virginia v. B.P.J. and Little v. Hecox, the Court ruled 6-3 (opinion by Justice Kavanaugh) that state laws restricting girls'/women's school sports teams to biological females do not violate the Equal Protection Clause; the Court was unanimous that the laws don't violate Title IX. Justices Sotomayor, Kagan, and Jackson dissented on the constitutional question.

media.caption: Supreme Court rules states may exclude transgender athletes from girls' and women's school sports

title: Supreme Court Strikes Down Limits on Party-Candidate Campaign Coordination Spending
detail: In National Republican Senatorial Committee v. FEC, the Court ruled 6-3 along ideological lines that federal limits on how much political parties may spend in coordination with their own candidates violate the First Amendment, overruling its 2001 precedent in FEC v. Colorado Republican Federal Campaign Committee. Justice Kavanaugh wrote the majority opinion; the case was brought by VP JD Vance and other GOP groups, and Trump called it a 'win for Republicans.'

media.caption: Voters at a Denver polling site on June 30, 2026, as the Supreme Court loosens campaign spending limits
